description.value: The study examined changes in whole-brain functional connectivity following right inferior frontal cortex fMRI neurofeedback in adolescents with ADHD, using Brodmann area 44 and 45 seed regions and comparing findings with a left parahippocampal neurofeedback control group.

spans.text: we were particularly interested in the effects of rIFC self-regulation training in ADHD on functional connectivity with other brain networks.

design.value: Randomized controlled trial with an rIFC-Neurofeedback group and a lPHG-Neurofeedback control group; functional connectivity was compared between the first and last neurofeedback runs using seed-based whole-brain correlation analyses.

spans.text: The original study was a randomized controlled trial testing the efficacy of fMRI-Neurofeedback of rIFC in 18 ADHD adolescents compared to a group of 13 ADHD adolescents who had to enhance another control region, the left parahippocampal gyrus.
